title: Taiwan's Foxconn reports 35% rise in Q2 profit on AI demand, beats forecasts

content_html:
TAIPEI, Aug 12 (Reuters) - Taiwan's Foxconn, the world's largest contract electronics maker, reported on Wednesday a 35% rise in second-quarter profit, beating analyst forecasts, on continued strong demand for AI, which it predicted would drive ‌growth this year.

Net profit for the April to June period for Nvidia's biggest server maker and Apple's top ‌iPhone assembler was T$59.97 billion ($1.86 billion), versus an LSEG consensus estimate of T$58.8 billion and compared with T$44.4 billion a year earlier.

In an earnings release, ​it stuck to its previous forecast of "strong" growth for revenue this year and said it also saw strong AI demand driving growth throughout the year. The company does not give numeric forecasts.

The company, formally called Hon Hai Precision Industry, said its cloud and networking products segment, which includes AI servers, accounted for 51% of second-quarter revenue, exceeding 50% for the first time, while its smart ‌consumer electronics products segment, which includes iPhones, accounted ⁠for 29%.

"AI-related business performance will continue to grow in the third quarter. Combined with ICT products entering their peak season in the second half of the year, we expect significant quarter-on-quarter growth ⁠and strong year-on-year growth," said rotating CEO Michael Chiang.

When asked about updates on Nvidia's latest Vera Rubin server products that Foxconn manufactures, Chiang said the AI server racks would enter mass-production preparation in the third quarter, with shipments expected to begin in the fourth quarter.

"We ​expect ​production volumes to increase gradually over the next several quarters, and ​it (Vera Rubin) will become our major product next year," ‌he said.

While customer demand remains very strong, Chiang cautioned that the key determinant for the overall AI server rack market next year will be how much CoWoS capacity chip companies are able to secure.

Foxconn's customers, including Nvidia, rely heavily on manufacturing by Taiwan's TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker. CoWoS, or Chip on Wafer on Substrate, is a key advanced packaging technology developed by TSMC used in AI chip production that has been constrained by tight capacity amid booming AI demand.

"The market currently ‌expects CoWoS capacity to grow by more than 50% next year, ​but how much of that can ultimately be translated into shipments of next-generation ​AI server racks will depend on chip supply," Chiang ​said.

CAPITAL EXPENDITURE

Foxconn expects its capital expenditure to continue growing and forecasts a 30% increase in 2026 ‌from a year earlier.

content_html_zh:
路透台北 8 月 12 日 - 全球最大电子产品代工制造商台湾富士康周三报告称，由于人工智能需求持续强劲，第二季度利润增长 35%，超出分析师预期，预计人工智能将推动今年的增长。

英伟达最大的服务器制造商和苹果最大的 iPhone 组装商 4 月至 6 月期间的净利润为 599.7 亿新台币（合 18.6 亿美元），而 LSEG 一致预期为 588 亿新台币，而去年同期为 444 亿新台币。

在财报发布中，​该公司坚持之前对今年收入“强劲”增长的预测，并表示强劲的人工智能需求也将推动全年增长。 该公司没有给出数字预测。

该公司的正式名称为鸿海精密工业，该公司表示，包括人工智能服务器在内的云和网络产品部门占第二季度收入的 51%，首次超过 50%，而包括 iPhone 在内的智能消费电子产品部门则占 29%。

“第三季度人工智能相关业务业绩将继续增长。 加上下半年ICT产品进入旺季，我们预计季度环比增长显着，同比增长强劲。”轮值首席执行官Michael Jiang表示。

当被问及富士康生产的英伟达最新Vera Rubin服务器产品的更新情况时，江先生表示，AI服务器机架将在第三季度进入量产准备，预计第四季度开始发货。

“我们预计未来几个季度的产量将逐渐增加，它（Vera Rubin）将成为我们明年的主要产品，”他说。

虽然客户需求仍然非常强劲，但Chiang警告说，明年整个AI服务器机架市场的关键决定因素将是芯片公司能够获得多少CoWoS容量。

包括英伟达在内的富士康客户严重依赖全球最大的代工芯片制造商台湾台积电的制造。 CoWoS（即 Chip on Wafer on Substrate）是台积电开发的用于 AI 芯片生产的关键先进封装技术，但在 AI 需求蓬勃发展的背景下，该技术一直受到产能紧张的限制。

“市场目前预计 CoWoS 产能明年将增长 50% 以上，但其中有多少最终能转化为下一代 AI 服务器机架的出货量将取决于芯片供应，”Chiang 说道。

资本支出

富士康预计其资本支出将继续增长，并预计 2026 年将同比增长 30%。
